holidays.name: April Fools' Day
holidays.description: The world's most gleefully suspicious day. Pranks, fake headlines and plastic spiders in the cereal box are all fair game, and trusting anyone before noon is risky. Brands, newsrooms and siblings all compete to pull off the most believable hoax.
holidays.origin: Nobody knows exactly where it began. Theories include the switch to the Gregorian calendar in the 1500s, when people who kept celebrating the old New Year in spring were teased as fools. Spring festivals of mischief are another candidate. A 1561 poem by Flemish writer Eduard de Dene is among the earliest written references to a day of April foolery.
holidays.funFact: In 1957 the BBC aired a straight-faced news segment about Swiss families harvesting spaghetti from trees. Many viewers phoned in asking how to grow their own.

holidays.name: National Sourdough Bread Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of the tangy, chewy, crackly-crusted loaf, and for the bubbly jar of starter that lives on your counter. Bakers feed their starters, bake a loaf and swap tips. Everyone else gets an excuse to buy a loaf and eat it warm with too much butter.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates one of the oldest forms of leavened bread, made by wild yeast and bacteria instead of packaged yeast.
holidays.funFact: Some sourdough starters are passed down for generations. Bakers sometimes name them and treat them like family pets.

holidays.name: National One Cent Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the humble penny, the small copper-colored coin that has spent decades in couch cushions, jars and wishing fountains. Dig out your loose change, spot a lucky penny or round up a few for a good cause.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It plays on the date, since April 1 can be read as the 'first' day and the 'one' cent that goes with it.
holidays.funFact: The U.S. penny has become famously expensive to make. Its production cost has long been higher than its face value, which fueled years of debate over retiring it.
